question.text: Per the current SEBI SSE framework (incorporating the April 15, 2026 circular), an NPO that is only REGISTERED on a Social Stock Exchange (without raising funds through it) may continue registration without raising funds for:

answer.text: One year from the date of registration.
A fixed period of two years from the date of registration, with no extension permitted.
Three years from the date of registration.
Two years from the date of registration, extendable by one additional year subject to Social Stock Exchange approval.

explanation.text: The Logic: The SIA workbook (pp.211–212) supports the original two-year period for NPOs registered on the SSE without raising funds. SEBI's April 15, 2026 modification circular now allows this two-year period to be extended by one additional year, subject to Social Stock Exchange approval. Upon final expiry without a listed project, the NPO ceases to be registered. The Trap: The "fixed two years with no extension" framing reflects the older rule and is now stale. One year and three years are distractors that don't align with either the workbook or the modification circular. Cross-Exam Context: NISM XXIII Topics 6 and 9 lean on the registration-period sunset rule; III-A compliance does not have this since it is SSE-specific.
